news_items.title: Define metrics once and keep them correct with the dbt Semantic Layer on Amazon Redshift
news_items.summary: Amazon Redshift has no native semantic layer, yet teams still need consistent, governed metric definitions across BI tools. This post shows how to define a metric once with the open-source dbt Semantic Layer (MetricFlow) on Amazon Redshift so it stays correct at any grain, and proves a non-additive weekly average comes out right ($280, not $550).
news_items.ai_generated_summary: The dbt Semantic Layer (MetricFlow) can be used on Amazon Redshift to define metrics once for consistent, governed definitions across BI tools. This approach ensures metrics, such as non-additive weekly averages, remain correct at any grain.
news_items.why_it_matters: This matters to data engineers as it addresses the challenge of maintaining consistent and accurate metric definitions across diverse BI tools, improving data governance and reliability.
